t: Duplicate Cluster Manager: a plain-language overview
title: Duplicate Cluster Manager: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Duplicate Cluster Manager does and why archives need it. A duplicate cluster manager hunts down records that describe the same thing twice — 'Jon Smith' and 'John Smith' at the same address. It groups each family of duplicates into a cluster and hands the cluster to a human for the final call. Duplicates get found; nothing gets auto-deleted.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Duplicate Cluster Manager works
title: How the Duplicate Cluster Manager works
description: Overview: what the Duplicate Cluster Manager does and why archives need it. Real managers use blocking to avoid all-pairs comparison (only compare records sharing a last name, ZIP, or phone prefix), fuzzy matching with Levenshtein or Jaro-Winkler similarity inside each block, and union-find to merge pairwise matches into clusters transitively. Each cluster gets a canonical-record proposal, a review queue ordered by cluster size and confidence, and merge/keep-both decisions are logged. Nothing is ever auto-deleted — the manager proposes, humans dispose.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Duplicate Cluster Manager works: the deep tour
title: How the Duplicate Cluster Manager works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Duplicate Cluster Manager does and why archives need it. Real managers use blocking to avoid all-pairs comparison (only compare records sharing a last name, ZIP, or phone prefix), fuzzy matching with Levenshtein or Jaro-Winkler similarity inside each block, and union-find to merge pairwise matches into clusters transitively. Each cluster gets a canonical-record proposal, a review queue ordered by cluster size and confidence, and merge/keep-both decisions are logged. Nothing is ever auto-deleted — the manager proposes, humans dispose. Advanced systems learn match thresholds from labeled pairs, handle multi-field weighting (name matters more than address), and detect split/merge errors where one cluster actually hides two entities. Quality is measured by pairwise precision/recall on labeled duplicate corpora. The limits are intentionally distinct records that look alike (twins, Jr/Sr) — those need human judgment, which is exactly why the manager is a review tool and never an auto-deleter.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
